pathway.title: Thryv Holdings, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: The continuing business does not cover its own fixed charges. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 11,934 thousand for the first nine months of 2026 was 0.61x interest expense of USD 19,629 thousand, and after deducting the USD 17,815 thousand of restructuring and integration expense that the adjusted measure adds back it was a loss of USD 5,881 thousand. The same add-back was USD 15,546 thousand a year earlier, so it recurs, and reported EBITDA was a loss of USD 111,282 thousand because of a USD 94,800 thousand goodwill impairment and other add-backs. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C4

Cash flow is weaker than earnings because the print business has been paying for the rest. Continuing operations used USD 37,867 thousand of operating cash in the first nine months of 2026 and, after USD 23,613 thousand of capital spending, free cash flow before debt service was a loss of USD 61,480 thousand, while the print business supplied USD 77,453 thousand of operating cash. The agreed price of USD 142.0 million is indicatively 1.38x that operating cash flow annualized, so the sale replaces the print cash flow with little more than a year of it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C5; calculation C15

Liquidity is below the next 12 months of scheduled amortization before the sale. Cash of USD 8,752 thousand and ABL capacity of USD 11,000 thousand total USD 19,752 thousand against USD 35,000 thousand of Term Loan amortization due within 12 months, twice the USD 17,500 thousand that was due in the 12 months after the 2025 year-end. The ABL is lent against print assets only and ends when the sale closes, and a replacement revolver is being sought but is not in place; net debt was USD 230,417 thousand at September 30, 2026, and pro forma net debt after the sale, expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, is not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 144; calculation C6; Financial foundation (CP-1)

The leverage covenant is the decisive near-term risk, and the sale itself triggers the forecast breach. The company expects to fail the Total Net Leverage Ratio test, capped at 3.0x, at the December 31, 2026 assessment because covenant EBITDA will exclude the Print Business and cap restructuring add-backs; a waiver needs a majority of lenders, of which a related party holds 40.0%. The company expects its cash, operating cash flow, sale proceeds and cost savings to fund operations for 12 months, but says it could not repay the Term Loan in full if it were accelerated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 58; Business & governance (CP-1A)

The sale cannot repair the balance sheet on its own. Of the USD 142.0 million price, the ABL of USD 17.6 million and USD 34.3 million of accrued tax liabilities come first, leaving at most USD 90.1 million, before costs and price adjustments, for a Term Loan of USD 227.5 million principal, or 39.60% of it, and the price can fall for each month that closing is delayed. The Term Loan balance after the sale is therefore not established. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation C8

SaaS growth is carried by conversions of Digital clients, not by demand. SaaS revenue rose 0.35% in the first nine months of 2026 and fell 3.35% in the third quarter, while the company says conversions in the last 12 months added about USD 16.4 million of SaaS revenue in nine months, so SaaS revenue before conversions fell about 4.44%. Seasoned net revenue retention fell to 89% from 94%, SaaS clients fell 5% and SaaS gross margin fell to 64.0% from 70.0% because converted clients pay nothing extra at conversion, although revenue per SaaS client rose 2% in the quarter. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C22

Reliance on cost savings is high, and the savings are targets. Management targets USD 50.0 million to USD 55.0 million of gross annualized savings, realised in full only from 2028, and expects a further USD 15.0 million to USD 20.0 million of restructuring cost, mostly in cash through 2027, against adjusted EBITDA of USD 11,934 thousand for nine months. The SaaS reporting unit's own forecasts were cut enough in 2026 to cause a USD 94.8 million goodwill impairment, which weakens the case for trusting forward targets. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 54

Financial policy is conservative in form, but creditors hold little control. No dividend has ever been paid, repurchases were USD 4,999 thousand in 2025 and none in the first nine months of 2026, and the Keap purchase was funded mainly with equity; the lender that holds 40.0% of the Term Loan is also a shareholder, so its incentives decide the waiver as much as any other lender's. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C21

Market access is untested. All debt floats on SOFR, the Term Loan at SOFR plus 6.75%, and a rise of 100 bp adds about USD 2.7 million of annual interest on March 31, 2026 debt; the Term Loan's fair value of USD 215,476 thousand at September 30, 2026 was 94.71% of principal but was measured before the going-concern disclosure of November 9, 2026. On the maturity ladder in Financial foundation, which infers equal quarterly installments, USD 148,750 thousand of Term Loan principal falls due on May 1, 2029, so refinancing depends on the business proving itself before then. Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C9; calculation C14; Financial foundation (CP-1)

runs.text: The strongest support is the cash value of the print sale. USD 142.0 million of cash is earmarked for the ABL, USD 34.3 million of accrued tax liabilities and part of the Term Loan, which would reduce debt and the interest burden if the sale closes, but no more than USD 90.1 million can reach the Term Loan before costs. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C8

SaaS profitability is improving and is the second support. SaaS adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 22,098 thousand from USD 16,726 thousand in the first nine months of 2026, a margin of 6.44% against 4.89%, after sales and marketing expense fell 18.62%, which shows costs can be cut. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C12; calculation C18

Revenue per SaaS client is rising and supports recurring revenue. Monthly revenue per SaaS client rose 2% in the third quarter and 8% in the nine months as price increases and add-on sales outweighed free conversions, so each remaining client is worth more even though there are fewer of them. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 44

The Term Loan is priced near principal and no debt matures before 2028. The Term Loan's fair value was 94.71% of principal at September 30, 2026, and the ABL that ends with the sale is the only facility due before the Term Loan matures on May 1, 2029. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C9

The largest weakness is the forecast covenant breach with substantial doubt about continuing as a going concern. The company expects to exceed the 3.0x Total Net Leverage Ratio at the December 31, 2026 test once covenant EBITDA excludes the Print Business, a breach would let lenders accelerate USD 227.5 million of principal, and a waiver needs a majority of lenders including a related party that holds 40.0%. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 24

The continuing business does not cover its interest or fund itself. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 11,934 thousand was 0.61x interest expense in the first nine months of 2026, and continuing free cash flow before debt service was a loss of USD 61,480 thousand, so debt service depended on a print cash flow that leaves with the sale. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C1; calculation C5

Liquidity is thin against amortization. Cash and ABL capacity of USD 19,752 thousand compare with USD 35,000 thousand of Term Loan amortization due within 12 months, and the ABL ends when the sale closes. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation C6

SaaS demand is weaker than revenue suggests. SaaS revenue rose 0.35% in nine months only because conversions of Digital clients added about USD 16.4 million, and seasoned net revenue retention fell to 89% from 94% while SaaS clients fell 5%. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C10; calculation C11

Earnings quality is low. FY2025 adjusted EBITDA was USD 60,586 thousand above reported EBITDA, restructuring and integration expense recurs, and a USD 94.8 million goodwill impairment followed lower forecasts for the SaaS unit. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C16; calculation C3

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The Print Business sale. On September 12, 2026 Thryv, Inc. agreed to sell its print yellow pages and white pages directories in the United States, Australia and New Zealand, their digital editions and the Australian online white pages to Coldwater YP, LLC, an affiliate of Carolwood, L.P., for a cash purchase price of USD 142.0 million, subject to customary adjustments that include a revenue-based reduction for each month closing is delayed. Closing is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, the business is presented as discontinued operations, and a transition services arrangement of 12 months, extendable by 2 months, is expected. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 63

Use of proceeds. The company expects to use the net proceeds to repay and terminate the ABL, which stood at USD 17.6 million at September 30, 2026, to pay USD 34.3 million of accrued tax liabilities that include interest to the expected payment date, and to repay part of the Term Loan. Because it expects to pay the tax liability and the ABL in full at closing, both are shown as current liabilities. The amount of Term Loan to be repaid is not stated. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 23

Debt issued in 2024. On May 1, 2024 Thryv, Inc. entered into a USD 350.0 million senior secured Term Loan, 40.0% held by a related party, that matures on May 1, 2029, bears interest at SOFR plus 6.75% and amortizes by USD 52.5 million a year for the first two years and USD 35.0 million a year after that, and an asset-based revolving credit facility that matures on May 1, 2028 at SOFR plus 2.50% to 2.75% and was described as USD 85.0 million in the 2024 annual report. The Term Loan is secured by all the assets of Thryv, Inc., certain subsidiaries and the Company and guaranteed by the Company and certain subsidiaries; its tests are a maximum total net leverage ratio of 3.0x and a minimum SaaS revenue level, and the ABL requires fixed charge coverage of at least 1.0x and excess availability of at least USD 8.5 million. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-K_2024-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 111

No new debt since then. No term debt was issued in 2025 or the first nine months of 2026; borrowings were limited to the ABL, USD 21.9 million of Term Loan prepayments were made in 2025 and USD 8,750 thousand was paid in the first nine months of 2026, and the company says it is seeking a new revolving credit facility to follow the ABL when the sale closes. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-K_2025-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 144; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 58; calculation C11

Acquisitions and equity funding. Thryv, Inc. bought Keap on October 31, 2024 for USD 77.0 million in cash net of USD 7.6 million of cash acquired, a figure the 2024 annual report gives as USD 76.9 million, and funded it with an underwritten offering that raised USD 76.8 million, USD 11.5 million more from the underwriter's option and USD 5.5 million of ABL borrowing; the 2023 purchase of Yellow in New Zealand cost USD 8.9 million in cash. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 134; 10-K_2024-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-K_2025-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 88; calculation C10

fields.value: The earnings history needed for leverage is split by the sale. The third-quarter 2026 report restates the first nine months of 2026 and 2025 without the Print Business, while the annual reports and the first two quarterly reports include it, and no source states a recast full year 2025. Reported EBITDA for 2025 of USD 91,260 thousand therefore includes earnings the company has agreed to sell, and a last-twelve-months figure at September 30, 2026 would mix perimeters, so leverage and cash interest cover at that date are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Net debt fell from USD 268,026 thousand at the 2024 year-end to USD 242,735 thousand at the 2025 year-end and USD 230,417 thousand at September 30, 2026, mainly as the Term Loan was amortised. Over the same span reported EBITDA fell from USD 91,260 thousand in 2025 to USD 64,904 thousand for the twelve months to June 30, 2026, which is why net leverage rose from 2.66x to 3.61x even as debt fell.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA is far below the company's adjusted measure because the company adds back large charges. In 2025 the gap was USD 60,586 thousand, and for the first nine months of 2026 the bridge from a reported loss to USD 11,934 thousand of adjusted EBITDA rests on a USD 94,800 thousand goodwill impairment, USD 17,815 thousand of restructuring and integration expense and USD 11,292 thousand of share-based pay. The company expects further restructuring costs through 2027, so the add-back behaves as a continuing cost rather than a one-off.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating cash flow shows the same split. For the first nine months of 2026 continuing operations used USD 37,867 thousand of operating cash and the print business supplied USD 77,453 thousand; with capital spending of USD 23,613 thousand, free cash flow before debt service was an outflow of USD 61,480 thousand on the continuing perimeter and an inflow of USD 15,973 thousand with the print business included. The print cash flow leaves with the sale.

fields.value: Cash interest exceeds the continuing business's adjusted EBITDA. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 11,934 thousand for the first nine months of 2026 covered cash interest paid of USD 20,274 thousand only 0.59x, although that interest figure is stated for the whole company and may include interest of the print business.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Near-term liquidity is below scheduled amortization before operating cash flow. Cash and ABL capacity total USD 19,752 thousand against USD 35,000 thousand of Term Loan amortization due within 12 months, and the sale proceeds are earmarked for the ABL, USD 34.3 million of accrued tax liabilities and part of the Term Loan. The ABL is lent against print receivables only, so it ends with the sale.

fields.value: Client prepayments and accrued taxes fund operations without interest. Contract liabilities of USD 24,789 thousand are services owed to clients, and accrued liabilities include USD 40,841 thousand of accrued taxes, of which the IRS matter is the main part; both are cash or service obligations that sit outside the debt figure. Finance leases, operating leases and pension obligations are also carried outside Total Debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the company's own adjusted EBITDA leverage looks moderate: net debt was 1.60x adjusted EBITDA at the 2025 year-end and 1.88x at June 30, 2026, and the company expects USD 50.0 million to USD 55.0 million of gross annualized savings from its restructuring. The strongest reading in the issuer's favour is that the impairment and share-based pay are not cash costs and that restructuring will stop, so adjusted EBITDA is the better guide to debt service.

fields.value: That reading would win if the company published a recast twelve-month adjusted EBITDA at September 30, 2026 above the earlier level, if the sale closed with net proceeds large enough to leave the remaining Term Loan covered, and if the lenders waived the leverage covenant. A recast twelve-month figure below the earlier one, a closing delayed by the monthly price reduction, or a refused waiver would confirm the weaker view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business, transaction, ownership and governance fact pack for Thryv Holdings, Inc. (issuer thry-1556739), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit_snapshot (Full credit assessment). Scope: what the company does, who controls it, what it has done with its capital and what transaction is pending, from five SEC filings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thryv is turning into a smaller software-only business, and its creditors will depend on SaaS earnings that are not yet proven at that scale, because the print directories that carried its cash flow are being sold while client numbers and retention fall. SaaS is already 91.22% of continuing revenue but grew only 0.35% in the first nine months of 2026, total clients fell 19% in a year and seasoned retention slipped to 89% from 94%. A related party holds both equity and 40.0% of the Term Loan, so it carries weight in any covenant waiver.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C3; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sale turns Thryv into a software business, but the SaaS share of revenue rose mostly because print was removed, not because SaaS grew. SaaS was 58.73% of 2025 revenue as originally reported and is 91.22% of continuing revenue for the first nine months of 2026, yet SaaS revenue was USD 343,242 thousand against USD 342,037 thousand a year earlier, a rise of 0.35%. Creditors lose the print cash flow and gain a business whose growth has not yet replaced it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 165; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 35; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SaaS demand is weakening beneath flat revenue. Total clients fell 19% and SaaS clients 5% between September 30, 2025 and September 30, 2026, and seasoned net revenue retention fell to 89% from 94% in the third quarter because downgrades and cancellations outran upsell after the company refocused its product strategy; third-quarter SaaS revenue fell 3.35%. A shrinking client base lowers the recurring revenue that supports debt service even though monthly revenue per SaaS client rose 2%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 42; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are being diluted by free conversions and are not yet recovering. SaaS gross margin fell to 64.0% in the first nine months from 70.0% because Digital clients were upgraded to SaaS at no charge, and the company expects USD 50.0 million to USD 55.0 million of gross annualized savings from restructuring to be realised in full only from 2028, with a further USD 15.0 million to USD 20.0 million of cost still to come. Until then creditors rely on the execution of cuts rather than on proven margin.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital allocation has been creditor-supportive in form but has not protected the balance sheet. The 2024 Keap purchase was funded mainly with equity of USD 76.8 million plus USD 11.5 million and USD 5.5 million of ABL borrowing, USD 21.9 million of Term Loan prepayments were made in 2025 and no dividend has ever been paid; against that, USD 4,999 thousand of shares were repurchased in 2025 while debt was high, and the SaaS reporting unit later needed a USD 94.8 million goodwill impairment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 91; 10-K_2025-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 144; 10-K_2025-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 85; 10-K_2025-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 20; calculation C10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Governance gives creditors visibility but little control. The Company is a holding company whose Term Loan borrower is Thryv, Inc.; the board is classified with staggered three-year terms, the chief executive officer is also chairman, and the filings name no controlling shareholder, but they leave directors' ownership and the identity of the related-party lender to a proxy statement that is not supplied. A covenant waiver needs a majority of lenders and the related party holds 40.0% of the Term Loan, so its incentives decide the outcome as much as any other lender's.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 80; 10-K_2025-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 169; 10-K_2025-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 172; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 56

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Disclosure is timely and candid on the going-concern risk but silent on the numbers lenders test. The company disclosed substantial doubt about continuing as a going concern and a forecast covenant breach in its third-quarter report, yet it prints no reported leverage ratio, no covenant EBITDA and no minimum SaaS revenue thresholds, and its third-quarter report omits market-risk disclosure as a smaller reporting company.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sale is the central transaction and is only partly visible. The price is USD 142.0 million and can be reduced for each month that closing is delayed, and the proceeds are earmarked for the ABL, USD 34.3 million of accrued tax liabilities and part of the Term Loan; the purchase agreement itself is not supplied, so the adjustment formula, the closing conditions and any holdback are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SaaS profitability is improving and SaaS now carries the group: SaaS Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 22,098 thousand in the first nine months of 2026 from USD 16,726 thousand, a margin of 6.44% against 4.89%, monthly revenue per SaaS client rose 8% over the nine months and price increases took effect in the second quarter of 2026. A buyer paying USD 142.0 million in cash for a declining print business also shows the legacy assets still have value, and clients converted free of charge were leaving at about the same rate as other SaaS clients in the first nine months of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: That would outweigh the weak client trend if seasoned retention returned toward 94%, if the sale closed on the stated terms and if the lenders waived the covenant on the current structure. A further fall in seasoned retention, a closing delayed by the monthly price reduction or a refused waiver would confirm the weaker view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The proxy statement is not supplied, so the conclusion that no controlling shareholder exists rests on the filings' silence; a named large holder would move the governance view toward a controlled-company reading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The sale agreement is not supplied, so the conclusion that proceeds reduce debt rests on the quarterly report's summary; a different closing condition or a larger price reduction would weaken it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Seasoned retention is reported only for the third quarter and leaves out clients acquired with Keap, and client counts are recast only for the two September dates, so the conclusion that SaaS demand is weakening rests on a short run of data; a stable fourth quarter would soften it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No source states the related-party lender's identity or equity stake, so the conclusion that its vote carries weight in a waiver rests on its 40.0% loan share alone.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Print Business sale. On September 12, 2026 Thryv, Inc. agreed to sell its print yellow pages and white pages directories in the United States, Australia and New Zealand, their digital editions and the Australian online white pages to Coldwater YP, LLC, an affiliate of Carolwood, L.P., for a cash purchase price of USD 142.0 million, subject to customary adjustments that include a revenue-based reduction for each month closing is delayed. Closing is expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, the business is presented as discontinued operations, and a transition services arrangement of 12 months, extendable by 2 months, is expected.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Use of proceeds. The company expects to use the net proceeds to repay and terminate the ABL, which stood at USD 17.6 million at September 30, 2026, to pay USD 34.3 million of accrued tax liabilities that include interest to the expected payment date, and to repay part of the Term Loan. Because it expects to pay the tax liability and the ABL in full at closing, both are shown as current liabilities. The amount of Term Loan to be repaid is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Debt issued in 2024. On May 1, 2024 Thryv, Inc. entered into a USD 350.0 million senior secured Term Loan, 40.0% held by a related party, that matures on May 1, 2029, bears interest at SOFR plus 6.75% and amortizes by USD 52.5 million a year for the first two years and USD 35.0 million a year after that, and an asset-based revolving credit facility that matures on May 1, 2028 at SOFR plus 2.50% to 2.75% and was described as USD 85.0 million in the 2024 annual report. The Term Loan is secured by all the assets of Thryv, Inc., certain subsidiaries and the Company and guaranteed by the Company and certain subsidiaries; its tests are a maximum total net leverage ratio of 3.0x and a minimum SaaS revenue level, and the ABL requires fixed charge coverage of at least 1.0x and excess availability of at least USD 8.5 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No new debt since then. No term debt was issued in 2025 or the first nine months of 2026; borrowings were limited to the ABL, USD 21.9 million of Term Loan prepayments were made in 2025 and USD 8,750 thousand was paid in the first nine months of 2026, and the company says it is seeking a new revolving credit facility to follow the ABL when the sale closes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Acquisitions and equity funding. Thryv, Inc. bought Keap on October 31, 2024 for USD 77.0 million in cash net of USD 7.6 million of cash acquired, a figure the 2024 annual report gives as USD 76.9 million, and funded it with an underwritten offering that raised USD 76.8 million, USD 11.5 million more from the underwriter's option and USD 5.5 million of ABL borrowing; the 2023 purchase of Yellow in New Zealand cost USD 8.9 million in cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit synthesis for Thryv Holdings, Inc. (issuer thry-1556739), as of 2026-11-18, pathway credit_snapshot (Full credit assessment). Scope: business quality, cash flow, liquidity, refinancing and the main downside path, built on the three earlier modules and five SEC filings. The module status is Ready with Limitations because the filings mix reporting perimeters and omit the loan agreements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thryv's fundamental credit profile is weak, and its near-term outcome depends on a lender waiver and the closing of the Print Business sale, because the software business that remains has not yet shown it can pay interest and amortization from its own cash flow. In the first nine months of 2026 continuing operations earned adjusted EBITDA of USD 11,934 thousand against interest expense of USD 19,629 thousand and used USD 37,867 thousand of operating cash, while the print business that supplied USD 77,453 thousand of operating cash leaves with the sale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 54; calculation C1; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash and available ABL capacity of USD 19,752 thousand compare with USD 35,000 thousand of Term Loan amortization due within 12 months. The company forecasts a breach of its leverage covenant once the sale closes and has disclosed substantial doubt about continuing as a going concern.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The continuing business does not cover its own fixed charges. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 11,934 thousand for the first nine months of 2026 was 0.61x interest expense of USD 19,629 thousand, and after deducting the USD 17,815 thousand of restructuring and integration expense that the adjusted measure adds back it was a loss of USD 5,881 thousand. The same add-back was USD 15,546 thousand a year earlier, so it recurs, and reported EBITDA was a loss of USD 111,282 thousand because of a USD 94,800 thousand goodwill impairment and other add-backs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 54; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C1; calculation C3; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash flow is weaker than earnings because the print business has been paying for the rest. Continuing operations used USD 37,867 thousand of operating cash in the first nine months of 2026 and, after USD 23,613 thousand of capital spending, free cash flow before debt service was a loss of USD 61,480 thousand, while the print business supplied USD 77,453 thousand of operating cash. The agreed price of USD 142.0 million is indicatively 1.38x that operating cash flow annualized, so the sale replaces the print cash flow with little more than a year of it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 10; calculation C5; calculation C15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is below the next 12 months of scheduled amortization before the sale. Cash of USD 8,752 thousand and ABL capacity of USD 11,000 thousand total USD 19,752 thousand against USD 35,000 thousand of Term Loan amortization due within 12 months, twice the USD 17,500 thousand that was due in the 12 months after the 2025 year-end. The ABL is lent against print assets only and ends when the sale closes, and a replacement revolver is being sought but is not in place; net debt was USD 230,417 thousand at September 30, 2026, and pro forma net debt after the sale, expected in the fourth quarter of 2026, is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 14; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 25; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 58; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 63; 10-K_2025-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 144; calculation C6; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The leverage covenant is the decisive near-term risk, and the sale itself triggers the forecast breach. The company expects to fail the Total Net Leverage Ratio test, capped at 3.0x, at the December 31, 2026 assessment because covenant EBITDA will exclude the Print Business and cap restructuring add-backs; a waiver needs a majority of lenders, of which a related party holds 40.0%. The company expects its cash, operating cash flow, sale proceeds and cost savings to fund operations for 12 months, but says it could not repay the Term Loan in full if it were accelerated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 24; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 57; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 58; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sale cannot repair the balance sheet on its own. Of the USD 142.0 million price, the ABL of USD 17.6 million and USD 34.3 million of accrued tax liabilities come first, leaving at most USD 90.1 million, before costs and price adjustments, for a Term Loan of USD 227.5 million principal, or 39.60% of it, and the price can fall for each month that closing is delayed. The Term Loan balance after the sale is therefore not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 63; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SaaS growth is carried by conversions of Digital clients, not by demand. SaaS revenue rose 0.35% in the first nine months of 2026 and fell 3.35% in the third quarter, while the company says conversions in the last 12 months added about USD 16.4 million of SaaS revenue in nine months, so SaaS revenue before conversions fell about 4.44%. Seasoned net revenue retention fell to 89% from 94%, SaaS clients fell 5% and SaaS gross margin fell to 64.0% from 70.0% because converted clients pay nothing extra at conversion, although revenue per SaaS client rose 2% in the quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 34; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C10; calculation C11; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reliance on cost savings is high, and the savings are targets. Management targets USD 50.0 million to USD 55.0 million of gross annualized savings, realised in full only from 2028, and expects a further USD 15.0 million to USD 20.0 million of restructuring cost, mostly in cash through 2027, against adjusted EBITDA of USD 11,934 thousand for nine months. The SaaS reporting unit's own forecasts were cut enough in 2026 to cause a USD 94.8 million goodwill impairment, which weakens the case for trusting forward targets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is conservative in form, but creditors hold little control. No dividend has ever been paid, repurchases were USD 4,999 thousand in 2025 and none in the first nine months of 2026, and the Keap purchase was funded mainly with equity; the lender that holds 40.0% of the Term Loan is also a shareholder, so its incentives decide the waiver as much as any other lender's.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 119; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C21

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Market access is untested. All debt floats on SOFR, the Term Loan at SOFR plus 6.75%, and a rise of 100 bp adds about USD 2.7 million of annual interest on March 31, 2026 debt; the Term Loan's fair value of USD 215,476 thousand at September 30, 2026 was 94.71% of principal but was measured before the going-concern disclosure of November 9, 2026. On the maturity ladder in Financial foundation, which infers equal quarterly installments, USD 148,750 thousand of Term Loan principal falls due on May 1, 2029, so refinancing depends on the business proving itself before then.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 23; calculation C9; calculation C14; Financial foundation (CP-1)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest case against a weak view is that the difficulty is a covenant definition and a timing problem, not a shortage of cash value. The company expects liquidity to suffice for 12 months if a waiver is given, the sale brings USD 142.0 million of cash against a Term Loan whose quarter-end fair value was 94.71% of principal, and the restructuring targets USD 50.0 million to USD 55.0 million of gross annualized savings against nine-month adjusted EBITDA of USD 11,934 thousand. SaaS adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 6.44% from 4.89%, the SaaS segment alone earned USD 22,098 thousand, 1.13x interest expense, because the shortfall sits in Marketing Services, which is being exited, and a lender that is also a shareholder has reason to waive rather than accelerate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 58; calculation C9; calculation C12; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: That case would win if the lenders waived the covenant on terms that keep the Term Loan outstanding, the sale closed at the stated price with most net proceeds applied to the Term Loan, a replacement revolver were signed and continuing operating cash flow turned positive before interest. A refused waiver, a closing delayed beyond the fourth quarter of 2026, or a further fall in seasoned retention below 89% would confirm the weaker view.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The company's forecast is the only evidence of covenant headroom, so the conclusion that a waiver is needed would change if the loan agreement's definition of covenant EBITDA allowed larger add-backs than the company expects.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Conversion revenue is stated by the company to the nearest USD 0.1 million and only for clients converted in the last 12 months, so the conclusion that SaaS revenue fell before conversions is approximate and would soften if earlier conversions were separated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Operating cash flow of the continuing business is available only for nine months, so the conclusion that it burns cash would change if working capital timing reversed in the fourth quarter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No peer set or rating is supplied, so the weak assessment rests on general leveraged-credit criteria for interest cover and liquidity, and could prove too harsh or too lenient against sector norms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest support is the cash value of the print sale. USD 142.0 million of cash is earmarked for the ABL, USD 34.3 million of accrued tax liabilities and part of the Term Loan, which would reduce debt and the interest burden if the sale closes, but no more than USD 90.1 million can reach the Term Loan before costs.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SaaS profitability is improving and is the second support. SaaS adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 22,098 thousand from USD 16,726 thousand in the first nine months of 2026, a margin of 6.44% against 4.89%, after sales and marketing expense fell 18.62%, which shows costs can be cut.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C12; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue per SaaS client is rising and supports recurring revenue. Monthly revenue per SaaS client rose 2% in the third quarter and 8% in the nine months as price increases and add-on sales outweighed free conversions, so each remaining client is worth more even though there are fewer of them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Term Loan is priced near principal and no debt matures before 2028. The Term Loan's fair value was 94.71% of principal at September 30, 2026, and the ABL that ends with the sale is the only facility due before the Term Loan matures on May 1, 2029.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The largest weakness is the forecast covenant breach with substantial doubt about continuing as a going concern. The company expects to exceed the 3.0x Total Net Leverage Ratio at the December 31, 2026 test once covenant EBITDA excludes the Print Business, a breach would let lenders accelerate USD 227.5 million of principal, and a waiver needs a majority of lenders including a related party that holds 40.0%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The continuing business does not cover its interest or fund itself. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 11,934 thousand was 0.61x interest expense in the first nine months of 2026, and continuing free cash flow before debt service was a loss of USD 61,480 thousand, so debt service depended on a print cash flow that leaves with the sale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 9; calculation C1; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is thin against amortization. Cash and ABL capacity of USD 19,752 thousand compare with USD 35,000 thousand of Term Loan amortization due within 12 months, and the ABL ends when the sale closes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: SaaS demand is weaker than revenue suggests. SaaS revenue rose 0.35% in nine months only because conversions of Digital clients added about USD 16.4 million, and seasoned net revenue retention fell to 89% from 94% while SaaS clients fell 5%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 40; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C10; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings quality is low. FY2025 adjusted EBITDA was USD 60,586 thousand above reported EBITDA, restructuring and integration expense recurs, and a USD 94.8 million goodwill impairment followed lower forecasts for the SaaS unit.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 55; calculation C16; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Thryv is a holding company whose operating subsidiary borrows the Term Loan, and after the print sale about 91.22% of continuing revenue is SaaS subscriptions sold to small businesses. Substantially all contracts last one year or less, so revenue is recurring but visible for about a year and rests on retention rather than on a contracted backlog, which weakens cash flow visibility and refinancing confidence.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 56; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No controlling stockholder is named, and one shareholder that holds 40.0% of the Term Loan is the party whose vote shapes any waiver; its identity and equity stake are not established. Cash reaches the holding company only through its operating subsidiary, which borrows the Term Loan secured by all the assets of the subsidiary, certain subsidiaries and the holding company and guaranteed by the holding company and certain subsidiaries, so the lenders hold the assets of the operating group and the holding company sits behind them.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is recurring, short-dated and discretionary for small businesses, and structurally declining in Marketing Services, whose revenue fell 58.29% in nine months as it is wound down by 2028. Price increases in the second quarter of 2026 and add-on sales lifted revenue per SaaS client 8% in nine months, but seasoned net revenue retention fell to 89% and SaaS revenue before conversions fell, so pricing power is being used against shrinking volume; no client exceeds 5% of receivables, which limits concentration risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 125; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C10; calculation C11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins cannot be assumed to hold under volume pressure. Sales and marketing expense fell 18.62% in nine months, which shows flexibility, but SaaS gross margin fell to 64.0% from 70.0% on free conversions, the company plans additional investment in its salesforce, and the restructuring program adds cash cost before savings that are realised in full only from 2028, so operating leverage works against creditors while revenue falls.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C18

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earnings do not turn into free cash flow for debt service. Capital spending of USD 23,613 thousand in nine months, 6.28% of continuing revenue, is the smaller drain; continuing operating cash flow was a loss of USD 37,867 thousand, cash interest paid was USD 20,274 thousand for the whole company, USD 33.9 million of accrued tax liabilities is due at the sale closing and pension contributions of about USD 7.6 million are expected for 2026, so cash conversion is negative until the savings arrive. Capital spending can be cut, with about USD 2.8 million expected for the rest of 2026, but that frees little cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 9; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 31; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 58; calculation C17; calculation C2; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is the force that matters most to credit: all-in-one competitors and point solution providers compete for the same small-business clients, and the fall in seasoned retention shows clients downgrading or leaving products that are no longer emphasised. Buyers sign contracts of one year or less, which limits pricing power; new technology and market entrants add to the pressure; supplier power, mainly traffic acquisition costs in the shrinking Marketing Services segment, is not a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 23; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 41; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 44

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest rates and currency are the external factors that change credit outcomes. Substantially all debt floats, so a rise of 100 bp adds about USD 2.7 million of annual interest on March 31, 2026 debt, which is large against adjusted EBITDA of USD 11,934 thousand for nine months, and the company reports exposure to the Australian and New Zealand dollars with Australia about 11.3% of revenue. Other political, social and technology factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-03-31_thry.htm.jsonl, page 44; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 35; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are SaaS margin improvement, a USD 142.0 million cash sale price, rising revenue per client and a Term Loan priced near principal. Weaknesses are the forecast covenant breach, negative continuing free cash flow, thin liquidity and falling retention. Opportunities are the USD 50.0 million to USD 55.0 million savings target, a replacement revolver and price increases; threats are a refused waiver, a delayed closing, further churn among converted clients and higher interest rates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 30; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 44; calculation C5; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Scale and market position is Weak: continuing revenue fell 10.67% in nine months and clients fell 19%. Competitive advantage is Weak: retention fell, although revenue per client rose. Business diversification is Average: a broad small-business client base and no client above 5% of receivables, but one platform and one country dominate. Cost and capex flexibility is Average: sales and marketing expense fell 18.62% but restructuring costs persist. Margin stability is Weak: SaaS gross margin fell to 64.0% from 70.0% and adjusted EBITDA margin was 3.17%. Free cash flow stability is Weak: continuing free cash flow before debt service was negative. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is Weak: going-concern doubt, an ABL that ends and no replacement revolver, though the Term Loan was priced near principal at quarter-end. Liquidity position is Weak against amortization. Financial policy and governance is Average: no dividend and candid disclosure, offset by a shareholder-lender and limited creditor control. The trend is weakening on cash flow and improving on SaaS profitability, and the main missing datapoints are covenant headroom, net proceeds and a recast twelve-month EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 35; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-Q_2026-09-30_thry.htm.jsonl, page 52; calculation C19; calculation C18; calculation C5; calculation C9; Business & governance (CP-1A)

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over 12 to 24 months the outcome is set by three events: the waiver, the sale closing and the replacement revolver; the company's own forecast breach and the end of the ABL make these the main headwinds, and the restructuring savings of USD 50.0 million to USD 55.0 million, full from 2028, are the main tailwind. Over three to five years the question is whether SaaS revenue can grow without free conversions once Marketing Services ends in 2028; management says small-business demand for integrated technology continues to grow, but retention, client counts and revenue before conversions all fell in 2026, so the sector tailwind is not yet visible in the issuer's results.

fields.value: The initiating condition is the sale closing while no waiver is in place, or a closing delayed past the fourth quarter of 2026 by the price adjustment. Covenant EBITDA then excludes the print business, the Total Net Leverage Ratio test at December 31, 2026 is breached, and the lenders may accelerate USD 227.5 million of Term Loan principal; the first operational break is the loss of the ABL, whose borrowing base is print assets only, which removes USD 11,000 thousand of capacity while a replacement revolver is not yet signed. Financial transmission follows: continuing operations used USD 37,867 thousand of operating cash in nine months, tax liabilities of USD 34.3 million take part of the proceeds, and cash of USD 8,752 thousand cannot repay the Term Loan, so the lenders, one of which is a shareholder holding 40.0% of the loan, would set the terms of any amendment. Management levers are the restructuring savings, capital spending of about USD 2.8 million for the rest of 2026 and working capital; they are too small and too slow to avoid a liquidity event if the Term Loan were accelerated, which the company itself says it could not repay. Observable triggers are the covenant waiver or amendment announcement, the sale closing, any replacement revolver and fourth-quarter operating cash flow.

fields.value: Overall, Thryv presents a weak business profile as a smaller software-only issuer supported by improving SaaS margins and the cash value of the print sale, but credit quality is constrained by negative continuing cash flow, thin liquidity and a forecast covenant breach. Cash-flow durability appears weak because adjusted EBITDA covers interest 0.61x and the print cash flow leaves with the sale. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the waiver, the net proceeds applied to the Term Loan and a replacement revolver; the primary downside path is a covenant default after the sale closes. Business profile against typical leveraged-credit issuers is not established because no peer set is supplied. Further analysis would require the loan agreement definitions, the sale agreement terms, net proceeds and a recast twelve-month earnings history.
